title: Apple bircher with grapes and hazelnuts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, apples, raisins, grapes, hazelnuts, lemon and cinnamon are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every item is an everyday line at Tesco at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a grater and a knife, with simple grating, stirring and chopping.

works.reason: 200g oats soaked in 500ml water with two grated apples gives a sensible set bircher for four, and the morning loosening step covers any thickness.

honest_times.reason: Grating two apples, squeezing a lemon, halving 300g grapes and chopping hazelnuts fits roughly ten minutes, and the 480 minutes is clearly the unattended overnight soak.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon and cinnamon, is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and only water is added.

seasonal_feel.reason: At 300g for four, the grapes are a generous fruit topping rather than a garnish, and an overnight bircher with autumn apples suits a quick November breakfast.

plain_voice.reason: The steps read plainly in British English and a beginner could follow them.

hearty_healthy.reason: Whole oats, fresh fruit and nuts make a filling, real-food breakfast that a family would happily eat again.
